stem: Why might the head circumference measurement be unreliable during the first few days of a newborn's life?

options.text: Rapid brain cell division occurs immediately after birth.
The presence of molding, cephalohematoma, or caput succedaneum.
The infant's inability to hold their head steady for the tape measure.
The cranial sutures have usually already fused at birth.

explanation: Mechanical changes to the head shape during delivery or localized swelling can temporarily distort the measurement.
rationale: Consider the physical effects of the birthing process on the shape and tissues of the infant's head.

optionExplanations.A: While the brain grows, it does not change size so drastically in days as to make measurements unreliable; the issue is mechanical.
optionExplanations.B: Mechanical changes to the head shape during delivery or localized swelling can temporarily distort the measurement.
optionExplanations.C: This is a practical difficulty for the clinician but does not make the measurement physiologically unreliable or inaccurate in terms of head volume.
optionExplanations.D: Cranial sutures remain open for the first two years of life to allow for brain expansion.

source.hint: Consider the physical effects of the birthing process on the shape and tissues of the infant's head.
